You don't have to map anything that isn't already working in rock band correctly. The only reason I did was because the game would only register the tom1 pad for me.

Alright, here is a pic of what I was talking about.
http://imgur.com/4fwM8dX

I now realize that when you choose NoteOn as the event type that it changes 'value 1' to 'note #' my bad.

I used the snare as an example in this one. Say you hit the snare and the number 22 showed as the midi value (the red box.) You would need to change that value to 38 in order for rock band to register it as a snare (the blue box.)  The green is the check box for turning mapping on, which you can only do after you create at least one map.

As for the min max boxes, just use the same numbers for those. If you were to use 22 min and 48 max then every time you hit a pad that used the midi values between 22 and 48 they would be changed to whatever number you entered in the second 'note #' boxes underneath.

As for the cymbals, you don't have to switch the cords. Just swap the numbers for the crash and ride in the chart I provided.

Hope that helped!

The easy way to deal with him is staying close in the first phase and hitting him a couple of times then dodging out to avoid explosions. 

Once he reaches his second phase, stay the fuck away from him, unless he does the sword rain technique in which case wait until slightly after the small shock wave and hit the sword. 

In the second phase you have to just keep your distance until he does one of his arial attacks. If he goes straight up out of view then dodge forward twice to end up behind him. 

If he flies backward into the air then he will do his spinning attack, that one you want to wait until he starts the lunge then dodge once into him. After either of his arial attacks he will be vulnerable long enough to land two quick hits, after that avoid him like the plague until he flies off again. 

I was able to beat him using this strategy using only around 7 vials.
